name: GMAT
fullName: Graduate Management Admission Test - GMAT Exam (Focus Edition; GMAC now also calls the current version the 11th Edition)
eligibility: You must be at least eighteen (18) years old to schedule and take the GMAT exam. Test takers aged thirteen (13) to seventeen (17) may take the exam at a test center if they give written proof of a parent's or guardian's consent before scheduling. GMAC sets no academic eligibility requirement.
mode: Computer-adaptive. Taken at a test center or online with a human proctor; both versions have the same structure, number of questions, timing, scoring algorithm and score scale.
frequency: Up to 5 attempts (test center and online combined) in a rolling 12-month period, with at least 16 days between attempts. GMAC has removed the earlier 8-attempt lifetime limit, so there is now no lifetime limit. Anyone who has scored a perfect 805 must wait 5 years before testing again.

pattern.marking: Total score 205-805, and every total ends in 5. Each section is scored 60-90, and the three sections count equally toward the total. Each section score depends on the number of questions answered, whether the answers are correct, and the difficulty and other parameters of those questions. In Data Insights, every part of a multi-part question must be correct to earn credit. No negative marking per question is stated.
pattern.notes: The exam lasts 2 hours 15 minutes and includes an optional 10-minute break after the first or second section. Test takers pick the section order. A calculator is available only in Data Insights. Totals cannot be compared directly with 10th Edition scores (200-800); compare using percentiles instead.

syllabusAreas: Quantitative Reasoning: Problem Solving questions on algebraic and arithmetic foundational knowledge and how it is applied to solve problems (no calculator)
Verbal Reasoning: Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning - reading and comprehending written material and reasoning about and evaluating arguments

Data Insights: Data Sufficiency, Multi-Source Reasoning, Table Analysis, Graphics Interpretation and Two-Part Analysis - analyzing and interpreting data and applying it to real-world business scenarios (on-screen calculator available)

registrationFee.category: Online exam (general price; GMAC says the exact cost varies slightly by location, and no India-specific online figure was retrievable)

keyDates.dateText: Year-round, on-demand (test center and online appointments)
Unofficial scores on screen right after the exam; Official Score Report about 3-5 days later (online exam, per GMAC)

scoreValidity: 5 years. Candidates can send scores to programmes for up to five years after the exam, and Official Score Reports show every exam taken in the past 5 years.
resultAndCounselling: Unofficial section and total scores appear right after the exam, and the Official Score Report follows, which the candidate sends to programmes. Schools that get scores electronically see them within about three weeks of the exam. Score reports list every exam from the past 5 years. Scores cancelled by GMAC carry notations (T, P or S) on the report. Across multiple attempts, GMAC's Superscore combines the best section scores into one score. There is no central counselling: each programme uses GMAT scores in its own admissions process, together with essays, academic history and interviews. For example, ISB requires a GMAT or GRE score but sets no minimum or cutoff.
